title: Give the points back after a crash

blocks.text: Cardholders can pay part of a purchase with loyalty points. `RedeemPoints`, in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/RedeemPoints.java`, takes the points off the loyalty account in `prepare` (field 48 says how many, field 102 names the account), and the loyalty service holds them until the server confirms or cancels the redemption. A purchase without field 48 uses no points.

Last month the server was restarted after a crash, and the loyalty team found redemptions that were neither confirmed nor cancelled, for purchases that never got an answer. The points are still gone from the cardholders' accounts.
The TransactionManager already journals to disk. Finish the two methods marked `TODO`:

items: `afterRedeem`, called once the service has redeemed the points;

blocks.text: About ten lines in total. The service is the `PointsService` interface at the top of the file.

The tests deploy a real TransactionManager with Q2 in the test's JVM, with a Berkeley DB journal. They play a crash by pausing a transaction at a later participant and never resuming it, then stop the TransactionManager and start it again, so that it recovers from its journal.

cases.says: a purchase that commits confirms its redemption once
a purchase declined after the redemption cancels it once
the journal holds the redemption only if the participant that changed the Context lets the TransactionManager snapshot it
only persisted entries reach the journal, so a redemption kept the ordinary way is lost in a crash
recovery calls abort on every participant of the chain, so a transaction that redeemed nothing must not reach the service

origin.section: 15.3 Recovery Aborts What Was Preparing and Commits Again What Was Committing

concepts: The TransactionManager journals each transaction's state and a snapshot of its persistent Context entries, after every participant that does not vote READONLY, in its persistent space, which is in memory unless a disk-backed space is named.
At start-up, a transaction left preparing is aborted and one left committing is committed again, on every participant of the chain, with only the persisted entries of the last snapshot.
